name: Equity: Devices, Internet, and Time
title: Equity: Devices, Internet, and Time
answer: Equity in personalized learning means making sure every student can actually use the tools, not just handing the same tool to everyone. The idea responds to the fact that personalized learning at home assumes a device and dependable internet, which many students do not have. It matters because a homework tool that only part of the class can reach tends to increase gaps rather than reduce them.

sections.body: This idea concerns the conditions that allow personalized learning to happen outside school. The problem is that home-based personalized learning assumes a device and dependable internet, and many students lack both. A homework tool available to only some students tends to widen gaps rather than close them. The idea also treats time and support as part of access, because a student with a quiet place to work and an adult to help will get more from any tool than a student caring for younger siblings in a crowded home. Equity, then, is about every student being able to gain from the tool, not about giving everyone the same tool.
sections.heading: The idea

sections.body: In practice, districts can lend devices and hotspots and keep libraries and computer labs open before and after school. Some districts give class time for work that other students do at home. Every personalized learning plan should say what happens for the student without internet at home. Teachers should design assignments that can be completed in school when needed. The supplied text does not divide these steps by grade band, so the same practical moves apply across grades.
sections.heading: How it works in school

sections.body: The text cites a study of nearly 4,500 sixth graders in the Netherlands. It found that family income affected achievement directly and that classroom AI use did not change that advantage (Wang et al., 2026). The book uses this finding to support its warning that a homework tool available to only some students tends to increase gaps rather than reduce them. No other study, figure, or finding appears in the supplied text.
sections.heading: What the evidence says

sections.body: The limits are practical and tied to unequal access. Personalized learning at home assumes a device and dependable internet, and many students lack both. A tool available to only some students can increase gaps, so districts and teachers must decide how to lend devices and hotspots, when to keep libraries and computer labs open, when to give class time for work others do at home, and what a plan will do for a student without internet. Time and support also matter, because a student with a quiet place and adult help will get more from any tool than a student caring for younger siblings in a crowded home. Teachers should design assignments that can be completed in school when needed, and the decision to ensure every student can benefit stays with the people running the school and classroom.
